To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed antibodies that inhibit AbetaP formation by blocking the beta-secretase processing of APP.

we have developed a novel approach to inhibit amyloid-beta peptide (a major component of the amyloid plaques found in the brains of Alzheimer's disease patients) production, by means of site-directed antibodies against the beta secretase cleavage site in the amyloid precursor.
we have developed a unique strategy to inhibit AbetaPP formation by means of antibodies to beta-secretase.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel inhibitors of beta-secretases that are based on antibodies directed to the beta-secretase APP site.
the development of a novel strategy for inhibiting the beta-secretase APP-cleaving enzyme, which is involved in amyloid-beta peptide production.
the development of novel approaches for the inhibition of beta-secretase and the subsequent reduction of AbetaP formation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the beta-secretase APP processing can be blocked by means of antibodies directed against the beta-secretases cleavage site of the APP, and that this inhibition can be achieved by means of site directed antibodies.
the antibodies presented here are able to bind APP in its native conformation in living cells and inhibit the beta-secretase activity.
site-directed antibodies to the beta-secretase processing site of APP can effectively interfere with the beta-secretase activity and inhibit AbetaP formation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
site-directed antibodies against the beta-cleavage site of APP can block AbetaP production, and therefore may be used as a potential therapeutic agent in Alzheimer's disease.
we have shown that antibodies against the beta secretase cleavage site can block beta secretase activity in vitro and in vivo.
we have developed a novel approach to inhibit Abbeta production by means of site-directed antibodies that interfere with APP processing by beta-secretases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the beta-secretase activity of BACE can be effectively blocked by means of site-directed antibodies.
the beta-secretase APP-cleaving site is a promising target for the development of anti-AbetaP antibodies that could serve as a therapeutic approach for the treatment of Alzheimer's disease.
the use of antibodies against the BACE cleavage site of the APP is a feasible approach for inhibiting AbetaP production and thus preventing Alzheimer's disease.
